t:
Which among the following constitute hind brain?
[[img:dcb15c13c6ed]]
s: The hindbrain consists of the pons, cerebellum and medulla oblongata. The pons connects different regions of the brain, the cerebellum coordinates movements and balance, and the medulla controls respiration and cardiovascular reflexes. Thalamus, hypothalamus and cerebrum are parts of the forebrain. Hence 2, 3 and 5.

t:
In the diagrammatic representation of the sectional view of cochlea, identify the part which ends at the oval window
[[img:eaa79f087409]]
s: In a cross section of the cochlea, the upper chamber (b) is the scala vestibuli, the lower (c) is the scala tympani, and the middle one is the scala media containing the organ of Corti. The scala vestibuli ends at the oval window, while the scala tympani ends at the round window opening to the middle ear. Hence b, scala vestibuli.

t: The junction between two neurons is
s: A synapse is the junction formed between the membranes of a pre-synaptic neuron and a post-synaptic neuron, which may or may not be separated by a synaptic cleft. Impulses are transmitted across it electrically or chemically. The motor end plate is a junction between neuron and muscle, while receptors and free nerve endings are sensory structures.

t: The part which connects brain to the spinal cord is
s: The medulla oblongata is the lowest part of the hindbrain and is continuous with the spinal cord, connecting the brain to it. It also contains centres controlling respiration, cardiovascular reflexes and gastric secretion. Hypothalamus, thalamus and amygdala are forebrain structures. Hence medulla oblongata.

t: The human brain weighs about:
s: The adult human brain weighs about 1.3 to 1.4 kg, i.e. about 1400 g, roughly 2% of body weight. It is protected by the cranium and meninges. The other values (800 g, 1000 g, 1800 g) do not correspond to the average adult human brain weight. Hence 1400 g.

t:
Select the correct match
[[img:b77014e2dd34]]
s: The brain acts as the central information processing organ, the command and control system (a-r). The CNS includes the brain and spinal cord (b-p). The ANS controls involuntary visceral organs and smooth muscles (c-q). The PNS includes the somatic and autonomic neural systems (d-s). Hence a-r, b-p, c-q, d-s.

t: Brain stem is composed of
s:
The brain stem forms the stalk-like lower part of the brain that connects the cerebrum with the spinal cord. According to human neuroanatomy, it is composed of three vital structures: the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata. 

Options (A) and (D) are incorrect because the hindbrain (rhombencephalon) includes the cerebellum, which is not considered a part of the brain stem. Option (C) is incorrect because it erroneously includes the cerebellum and excludes the medulla oblongata. 

Correct Answer: (B) Midbrain, pons and Medulla oblongata

t:
Diagrammatic representation of knee jerk reflex is shown below. Identify the parts labelled as A, B, C, D.
[[img:fcb84ba4a63b]]
s: In the knee jerk reflex, tapping the tendon stretches the thigh muscle, whose stretch receptors (B) are stimulated. The afferent sensory pathway (D) carries the impulse to the spinal cord, where it synapses with a motor neuron (E) in the ventral horn. The efferent pathway (C) carries impulses back to the effector muscle (A), which contracts. Hence option B.
o: Receptor - B, Effector - A, Motor Neuron - D, Efferent pathway - C, Afferent pathway - E
Motor Neuron - E, Afferent pathway - D, Efferent pathway - C, Effector - A, Receptor - B
Receptor - A, Effector - B, Afferent pathway - C, Efferent pathway - D, Motor Neuron - E
Motor Neuron - A, Receptor - B, Effector - E, Efferent pathway - C, Afferent pathway - D

t: In a resting neuron , the axoplasamic side of axolemma has
s: In a resting neuron the axolemma is more permeable to K⁺ than Na⁺ and impermeable to negatively charged proteins in the axoplasm. The axoplasm has high K⁺, low Na⁺ and many negatively charged proteins, so the inner side is negative relative to outside (polarised). Hence C; options A, B and D misstate the charges or concentrations.
o: A positive charge due to potassium ions
A low concentration of K- ions and a high concentration of Na- ions
A negative charge due to negatively charged proteins
An equal concentration of Na and K- ions

t: Respiratory centres are located in: -
s: The respiratory rhythm centre lies in the medulla oblongata, and the pneumotaxic centre in the pons modulates it by shortening inspiration and altering rate. Together these hindbrain regions regulate breathing. The cerebellum coordinates movement, and the thalamus and corpus callosum are forebrain structures. Hence medulla oblongata and pons.

t: Nissl's granules are absent in
s: Nissl's granules are clusters of rough ER and ribosomes present in the cyton (cell body) and also in dendrites. They are absent from the axon and the axon hillock, which is why axons depend on the cell body for protein synthesis. Hence axon, option A.

t: In a neuron, conversion of electrical signal to a chemical signal occurs at/in
s: When an impulse reaches the axon terminal, it causes synaptic vesicles to fuse with the presynaptic membrane and release neurotransmitter into the synaptic cleft. Here the electrical signal is converted into a chemical signal, which binds receptors on the postsynaptic membrane to regenerate an electrical signal. Hence presynaptic membrane.

t:
Find the correct match
[[img:dcbcd094b61c]]
s: Multipolar neurons with one axon and many dendrites occur in the cerebral cortex (a-n). Bipolar neurons are found in the retina (b-p). Nodes of Ranvier are gaps on myelinated axons (c-k). Apolar neurons occur in coelenterates (d-m). Unipolar neurons are typically found in the embryonic stage (e-l). Hence option C.

t: All are true regarding axoplasm inside a resting neuron except
s: In a resting neuron the axoplasm contains a high concentration of K⁺ and negatively charged proteins and a low concentration of Na⁺, while the extracellular fluid has low K⁺ and high Na⁺. So low K⁺ and high Na⁺ inside is incorrect; it describes the outside fluid. Hence C.
o: low level of K⁺and high level of Na⁺

t: Schwann cells
s: Schwann cells are neuroglial cells of the peripheral nervous system that wrap around axons to form the myelin sheath, interrupted at nodes of Ranvier. In the CNS, myelin is formed by oligodendrocytes, phagocytosis is by microglia, and astrocytes help regulate the blood–brain barrier. Hence D.

t:
Match the following and select the correct one
[[img:1f0a052d2f60]]
s: Resting potential is the potential difference across the resting (polarised) membrane (a-r). Action potential is the potential difference across a depolarised membrane (b-p). Blocking the Na⁺–K⁺ pump stops Na⁺ extrusion, so Na⁺ increases in the axoplasm (c-s). Hyperpolarisation results from slow closing of K⁺ channels, letting excess K⁺ leave (d-q). Hence option A.

t: The most abundant neurotransmitter in man is
s: Among the options, acetylcholine is the most widely distributed neurotransmitter in humans: it is used at all neuromuscular junctions, at all autonomic ganglia, by parasympathetic postganglionic fibres and in many brain pathways. Adrenaline, dopamine and histamine are restricted to fewer specific pathways. Hence acetylcholine.

t: Find the wrong statement
s: The cerebral aqueduct (iter) is a narrow canal in the midbrain connecting the third ventricle of the forebrain with the fourth ventricle of the hindbrain, not the neural canal with the central canal. Thalamus and hypothalamus are forebrain parts, the longitudinal fissure separates the hemispheres, and the corpus callosum occurs only in placental mammals. Hence B.
o: Thalamus and hypothalamus are parts of forebrain
Cerebral aqueduct is midbrain canal connecting neural canal and central canal
The longitudinal fissure seperates the 2 cerebral hemispheres
Corpus callosum, connecting the two cerebral hemispheres is found in placental mammals only

t: The dorsal portion of the midbrain consists mainly of four round swellings called
s: The midbrain lies between the forebrain and hindbrain. Its dorsal portion bears four round swellings (lobes) called corpora quadrigemina, two concerned with visual and two with auditory reflexes. The cerebral aqueduct is the canal through the midbrain, the cerebellum is in the hindbrain, and the corpus callosum joins the cerebral hemispheres. Hence D.

t: An injury to hypothalamus results in
s: The hypothalamus contains centres that control body temperature, hunger, thirst and hormone secretion via neurosecretory cells. Injury to it disrupts thermoregulation. Short-term memory is linked to the limbic system and cortex, consciousness to the reticular formation and cortex, and coordination of locomotion to the cerebellum. Hence D.

t: Which of the following is incorrect?
s: Corpus callosum is a broad band of nerve fibres that connects the left and right cerebral hemispheres, not the cerebellar hemispheres, so statement D is incorrect. The other statements are correct: the midbrain integrates visual, tactile and auditory inputs, the cerebellum integrates impulses from the inner ear for balance, and the cerebrum controls fine, skilful voluntary movements.
o: Midbrain receives and integrates visual, tactile and auditory inputs
Cerebellum integrates impulses from inner ear
Cerebrum integrates fine and skilful voluntary movements
Corpus callosum interconnects the cerebellar hemispheres

t:
Find the correct match

s: Corpora quadrigemina of the midbrain act as the centre for visual and auditory reflexes (a-r). The limbic system controls emotions and is called the emotional brain (b-p). The cerebellum is the little cerebrum (c-s). The thalamus relays sensory signals to the cortex and is the gateway to the cerebral cortex (d-q). So the order is r, p, s, q.

t: During the transmission of nerve impulse through a nerve fibre, the changes in electricl charges on the inner side of the plasma membrane is,
s: At rest the inner side of the axon membrane is negative. When an impulse arrives, Na⁺ rushes in and the inside becomes positive (depolarisation). Then K⁺ moves out, restoring the negative charge inside (repolarisation). So the inner side goes negative, then positive, then back to negative. The other options leave out the return to the resting state or start from the wrong charge.
o: First positive, then negative and continue to be negative.
First negative, then positive and continue to be positive.
First positive, then negative and again back to positive.
First negative, then positive and again back to negative

t: Identify the false statement.
s: An action potential is caused by the influx (entry) of Na⁺ into the axon, not its efflux, so statement A is false. During depolarisation the membrane polarity is reversed (inside becomes positive). Repolarisation is due to the efflux of K⁺. The impulse travels along the fibre as a wave of action potentials. So B, C and D are true.
o: Action potential is due to efflux of Na+
In depolarisation, polarity of membrane is reversed
Repolarisation is due to the efflux of K+
Impulse is transmitted as action potential

t: Sensory, association and motor areas of brain are located in
s: The cerebral cortex is the grey matter covering the cerebrum. It contains motor areas, sensory areas and large association areas that carry out complex functions such as memory, intersensory association and communication. The cerebral medulla is white matter made of fibre tracts. The cerebellar cortex deals with balance and coordination, and the thalamus is a relay centre.

t: The posterior most part of brain is:
s: The medulla oblongata is the last part of the hindbrain and continues into the spinal cord, so it is the posterior-most part of the brain. The olfactory lobes are at the anterior end of the forebrain. The pons and cerebellum lie in front of the medulla, so they are not the most posterior part.

t: Integration of informations from semi circular canals is done in
s: The semicircular canals of the inner ear sense rotation and changes in body position. Their impulses go to the cerebellum, which integrates them with other inputs to keep balance, posture and equilibrium. The thalamus is a sensory relay station, the hypothalamus controls homeostasis, and the corpora quadrigemina handle visual and auditory reflexes.

t: Faster conduction in myelinated fibres is due to
s: In myelinated fibres the myelin sheath insulates the axon, and ion exchange can happen only at the nodes of Ranvier. The impulse therefore jumps from node to node (saltatory conduction), which is much faster. It is not due to more ion channels or continuous depolarisation, which happen in non-myelinated fibres. A longer synaptic delay would slow conduction.

t: Which of the following is not true about chemical synapse
s: At a chemical synapse the impulse is carried across the synaptic cleft by neurotransmitters, so there is a synaptic delay and transmission is one-way (axon to dendron). This is not like conduction along an axon. Transmission along an axon is purely electrical and is seen only at electrical synapses, so statement A is not true for a chemical synapse.
o: Transmission is as along an axon
Conduction is only in axon dendron direction

t: Which brain structure is known as the "relay station" for sensory information?
s: The thalamus, in the diencephalon, receives almost all sensory impulses (except smell) and relays them to the right areas of the cerebral cortex, so it is called the relay station. The hypothalamus controls body temperature, hunger and hormones. The pons relays signals between the cerebrum and cerebellum and helps regulate breathing. The basal ganglia take part in motor control.

t: The branched tree-like structure/tree of life present in the cerebellum is
s: In a section of the cerebellum, the white matter branches like a tree inside the grey matter cortex. This pattern is called arbor vitae (tree of life). Arboreal means living in trees, archenteron is the primitive gut of the gastrula, and an areola is a small area such as the pigmented ring around the nipple.

t: Cerebrospinal fluid occurs
s: The three meninges are the outer dura mater, the middle arachnoid and the inner pia mater. Cerebrospinal fluid fills the subarachnoid space between the arachnoid and pia mater, and also the brain ventricles and the central canal. It cushions the brain against shock. The space between dura and arachnoid is the subdural space, which holds little fluid.

t:
Match the column I and column II and choose the correct combination from the options given.
[[img:cd9b04b9088a]]
s: The cerebrum is part of the forebrain (A-iii). The pons is part of the hindbrain (B-iv). The cerebral aqueduct is the canal passing through the midbrain (C-ii). The spinal cord, together with the brain, forms the central nervous system (D-i). So the correct combination is A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i.

t: Which of the following pairs is mismatched?
s: The pneumotaxic centre is in the pons, not the medulla oblongata, so pair C is mismatched. The medulla has the respiratory rhythm centre and also the cardiovascular centres. The other pairs are correct: the cerebrum controls voluntary activities, the cerebellum maintains body balance, and the spinal cord is the centre for spinal reflex actions.

t:
Match the column I and Column II and choose the correct combination from the options given.
[[img:14a4f8f371ad]]
s: The thalamus belongs to the forebrain (diencephalon) (A-iii). The brain stem is made of the midbrain, pons and medulla (B-iv). The hypothalamus lies at the base of the thalamus (C-i). The corpora quadrigemina are four lobes on the dorsal side of the midbrain (D-ii). So the correct combination is A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

t: Pre-excitation potential difference between outside and inside of a nerve is called
s: Before stimulation, the axon membrane has a potential difference of about -70 mV, with the inside negative compared with the outside. This is called the resting potential. It is kept by the Na⁺-K⁺ pump and by the membrane being more permeable to K⁺. The action (spike) potential develops only after a stimulus, and 'reaction potential' is not a standard term.

t: Depolarisation of nerve impulse involves
s: Depolarisation happens when a stimulus makes the membrane freely permeable to Na⁺. Na⁺ rushes in and the inside becomes positive. The exit of K⁺ happens in the next phase, repolarisation, so options C and D mix up two phases. K⁺ does not enter during depolarisation, so B is wrong. Only Na⁺ entry causes depolarisation.
o: Entry of Na⁺and exit of K⁺
Entry of K⁺and exit of Na⁺

t: In a nerve, if sodium pump is blocked, which of the following is most likely to happen?
s: The Na⁺-K⁺ pump uses ATP to move 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ into the cell. If it is blocked, Na⁺ that leaks in is no longer pumped out, so Na⁺ builds up inside the nerve. At the same time K⁺ leaks out and is not brought back, so K⁺ inside falls. So Na⁺ inside the nerve will increase.
o: Na⁺and K⁺will increase outside the cell

t: Which of the following statements is correct?
s: At a chemical synapse, the neurotransmitter binds to receptors on the post-synaptic membrane and produces a new potential that may be excitatory or inhibitory, so B is correct. Electrical synapses are rare in our body, so A is wrong. The thalamus, not the hypothalamus, is the major centre for sensory and motor signalling, so C is wrong. The cerebral hemispheres are joined by the corpus callosum, so D is wrong.
o: Electrical synapses are more common in our neural system than chemical synapses
The new potential in post-synaptic neuron may be either excitatory or inhibitory
Hypothalamus is the major coordination centre for sensory and motor signaling
The tracts of nerve fibres that connect two cerebral hemispheres are called corpous bigemina

t: Thermoregulatory centre or thermostat in the body of homeothermal animals and man is found in:
s: The hypothalamus has the thermoregulatory centre that acts as the body's thermostat. It senses blood temperature and starts sweating, vasodilation, shivering and other responses to keep body temperature constant. The hypothalamus is part of the diencephalon, but option C names the exact structure. The skin only has temperature receptors, and the pituitary is an endocrine gland.

t: The amount of neurotransmitter released from a presynaptic cell is a function of
s: Action potentials follow the all-or-none law, so every spike has the same voltage. The neuron codes signal strength by how often it fires. A higher frequency of action potentials arriving at the terminal lets in more Ca²⁺, which releases more neurotransmitter. Whether the effect is excitatory or inhibitory depends on the postsynaptic receptors, not on how much transmitter is released.
o: The voltage of the individual action potential in the presynaptic neuron
The frequency of arriving action potentials is the presynaptic neuron
Whether the action potential is excitatory or inhibitory
The receptors in the postsynaptic cell

t: Which of the following regions of the brain is incorrectly paired with its function?
s: Language comprehension is a function of the cerebral cortex (Wernicke's area), not the cerebellum. The cerebellum coordinates movement, posture and balance, so pair A is wrong. The corpus callosum connects the two cerebral hemispheres, the cerebrum handles calculation and thinking, and the medulla controls breathing, heart rate and other homeostatic functions, so those pairs are correct.
o: Corpus callosum - Communication between left \& right cerebral cortices

t: In a medullated nerve fibre, conduction of impulse is faster due to:
s: In medullated fibres the myelin sheath acts as an insulator, and the gaps between sheath segments, the nodes of Ranvier, are the only places where depolarisation can happen. The impulse jumps from node to node (saltatory conduction), so it travels faster. Pericytes surround capillaries, the endoneurium and epineurium are connective tissue coverings, and Nissl granules are used for protein synthesis.
o: Myelin sheath and Nodes of Ranvier

t: In a nerve cell, potassium concentration is:
s:
Correct Answer: (C) More concentrated inside

Explanation:
In a resting neuron, the intracellular fluid (axoplasm) has a high concentration of potassium ions (K+) and negatively charged proteins, but a low concentration of sodium ions (Na+). This ionic concentration gradient across the resting membrane is actively maintained by the Na+/K+ ATPase pump, which pumps 3 Na+ outwards for every 2 K+ into the cell. Consequently, K+ is more concentrated inside the cell membrane.

Why other options are incorrect:
- Options (A) and (B) are incorrect because it is sodium (Na+), not potassium (K+), that is more concentrated on the outside and less on the inside.
- Option (D) is incorrect because an unequal distribution of ions is essential to maintain the resting membrane potential.
o: Greater on the outside of membrane
Equal on both sides of membrane

t: Brain stem is made of:
s: The brain stem connects the brain to the spinal cord. It is made of the midbrain and the hindbrain parts pons and medulla oblongata. The cerebellum is part of the hindbrain but is not included in the brain stem. The diencephalon and cerebrum belong to the forebrain. So the brain stem is the midbrain plus the hindbrain without the cerebellum.
o: Midbrain and hind brain without cerebellum

t: Which of the following is the correct direction of travel for a nervous impulse?
s: Dendrites receive stimuli and carry impulses towards the cell body (cyton). The axon then carries impulses away from the cell body to the synaptic knobs. So the impulse travels dendrite → cell body → axon. The other sequences reverse this physiological direction, which is fixed because neurotransmitter is released only from axon terminals.

t:
Match the column I and column II and choose the correct combination from the options given :
[[img:10934e988643]]
s: The cerebellum maintains posture and balance (A-iv). The thalamus is the major centre for sensory and motor signalling (B-ii). Many reflex actions such as coughing, sneezing and vomiting are controlled by the medulla oblongata (C-iii). The cerebral hemispheres control voluntary actions and intelligence (D-i). So the correct combination is A-iv, B-ii, C-iii, D-i.

t: Primary function of myelin sheath around vertebrate axon is to
s: The myelin sheath, made by Schwann cells, insulates the axon and stops current from leaking out. Depolarisation can occur only at the nodes of Ranvier, so the impulse jumps from node to node and conduction becomes much faster. Myelin does not control the Na-K pump, does not increase the size of the action potential (which is all-or-none), and does not affect neurotransmitter release.
o: Increase in size of action potential
Increase in speed of conduction by preventing leakage of nerve impulse

t: Transmission of a nerve impulse is unidirectional due to:
s: Neurotransmitters are stored in synaptic vesicles only in the axon terminals, and receptors are present only on the post-synaptic membrane. So at a synapse the impulse can pass only from the axon of one neuron to the dendrite or cell body of the next. This makes transmission one-way. Myelin only speeds conduction, dendrites do not release transmitters, and the sodium pump does not travel along the axon.
o: Insulation of nerve fibre by medullary sheath
Neurotransmitters released only at axon ending
Neurotransmitters released only at dendrite ends
Sodium pump starts from cyton and proceeds to axon end

t: During transmission of nerve impulse through a nerve fibre, potential on the inner side of plasma membrane would changes:
s: At rest the inside of the membrane is negative. During depolarisation Na⁺ comes in and the inside becomes positive. During repolarisation K⁺ goes out and the inside becomes negative again. So the potential on the inner side changes from negative to positive and back to negative. The other options either do not return to the resting state or start from the wrong charge.
o: First negative, then positive and continue to be positive
First positive, then negative and continue to be negative
First positive, then negative and again back to positive
First negative, then positive and again back to negative

t: During conduction of nerve impulse, the action potential is the result of movement of:
s: When a stimulus is applied, Na⁺ channels open. Na⁺, which is more concentrated outside, rushes from the extracellular fluid into the intracellular fluid. This reverses the membrane polarity and creates the action potential. Na⁺ moves out only through the Na⁺-K⁺ pump during recovery, and K⁺ efflux causes repolarisation, not the action potential.
o: Na⁺from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid
Na⁺from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid

s: B and C are correct: Schwann cells form the myelin sheath around myelinated fibres and also enclose non-myelinated fibres without forming myelin. A is wrong because neurotransmitters such as adrenaline are released by synaptic knobs (axon terminals), not by the cleft. D is wrong because spinal and cranial nerves contain myelinated fibres. t:
Statement-I : The functions of muscles, lungs, heart, blood vessels, kidneys and other organs are coordinated while performing physical exercise.
Statement-II : In our body, the neural system and endocrine system jointly coordinate all activities of organs so that they function in a synchronised fashion.
s: Both statements come from NCERT. During exercise, muscles, lungs, heart, blood vessels and kidneys must work together, with more oxygen supply, a faster heart rate and changes in blood flow. This coordination is carried out jointly by the neural system and the endocrine system, which keep organ functions synchronised. So both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.

t: Which of the following is not correct with respect to the neural system of the insects?
s: The insect neural system is made of a brain and many ganglia along a ventral nerve cord, so it is better organised than the simple nerve net of Hydra. Statement B, that it is simply a network of neurons, describes Hydra and not insects, so B is incorrect. The other statements are true for insects.

t:
Match the following types of neurons with their descriptions:
[[img:0cdb66ccf70e]]
s: A multipolar neuron has one axon and many dendrites (A-iii). A bipolar neuron has two processes, one axon and one dendrite (B-i). So the correct match is A-iii, B-i, C-iv, D-ii.

t: In the resting stage of neuron, concentration gradient generates due to
s: At rest the axoplasm has a high concentration of K⁺ and negatively charged proteins and a low concentration of Na⁺. The extracellular fluid has a high concentration of Na⁺ and a low concentration of K⁺. These opposite gradients are kept by the Na⁺-K⁺ pump and set up the resting potential. Options B, C and D describe the ion distribution the wrong way round.
o: High concentration of K⁺and low concentration of Na⁺inside the axon
High concentration of Na⁺and low concentration of K⁺inside the axon

t:
Given below are steps in the generation and conduction of nerve impulse. Arrange them in proper sequence:
A) Rapid influx of Na⁺ions followed by reversal of polarity at the site of application of stimulus.
B) Reversal of polarity and generation of action potential at a point ahead of the point of application of stimulus.
C) Development of free permeability to Na⁺ions at the site of application of stimulus.
D) Arrival of the impulse generated at the first site to the second site.
E) Rise in permeability of K⁺ions and restoration of the resting potential of the membrane.
s: First, the stimulus makes the membrane freely permeable to Na⁺ (C). Na⁺ rushes in and the polarity reverses at the stimulated site (A). Local current flows to the next site (D's region), where the polarity also reverses and an action potential is generated (B). The impulse arrives at the second site (D). Finally, rising K⁺ permeability restores the resting potential (E). The order is C, A, B, D, E.

t: All statements about electrical synapses are correct except:
s: In electrical synapses the pre- and post-synaptic membranes are very close together and are joined by gap junctions. Current flows directly, so transmission is like conduction along a single axon and is faster than at a chemical synapse. However, electrical synapses are rare in our system and most synapses are chemical, so statement D is the exception.
o: The membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity
Transmission of impulse across this synapse is very similar to impulse conduction along a single axon
Impulse transmission is always faster than that across a chemical synapse
Electrical synapses are very common in our body

t:
Select the correct options:
(A) Grey matter is internal and surrounded by white matter in spinal cord.
(B) White matter is outside in the brain.
(C ) Cerebellar hemisphere shows a tree-like arrangement of grey matter called arbor vitae.
(D) The ependymal cells are columnar epithelial cells.
(E) Corpora quadrigemina is present in Rhombencephalon.
(F) Alcohol affects the hypothalamus.
s:
Correct Answer: (B) (A), (C ), (D) and (F)

Explanation:
- Statement (A) is correct because in the spinal cord, grey matter is centrally located (butterfly-shaped) and surrounded by outer white matter.
- Statement (C) is considered correct as the branching pattern in the cerebellum is known as the arbor vitae (tree of life).
- Statement (D) is correct because ependymal cells are ciliated cuboidal to columnar epithelial cells lining the brain ventricles and central canal.
- Statement (F) is correct because alcohol affects the hypothalamus, inhibiting ADH secretion and causing diuresis.

Why other statements are incorrect:
- (B) is incorrect because white matter is located internally (deep) in the brain, while grey matter forms the outer cortex.
- (E) is incorrect because the corpora quadrigemina is part of the midbrain (mesencephalon), not the hindbrain (rhombencephalon).

t:
Select the correct options:
(A) There are two types of synapses - electrical and chemical synapses.
(B) Electrical synapses are fast.
(C ) Neurotransmitters are involved in transmission of impulses at electrical synapses.
(D) In myelinated nerve fibres impulses jump from one node of Ranvier to another which is called saltatory propagation.
s: A is correct: synapses are either electrical or chemical. B is correct: electrical synapses are fast because current passes directly through gap junctions. D is correct: in myelinated fibres the impulse jumps from node to node, which is saltatory conduction. C is wrong because neurotransmitters are used only at chemical synapses. So the correct statements are A, B and D.

t:
Read the following statements and select the correct ones:
(A) Autonomic neural system transmits impulses from the CNS to voluntary organs and striated muscles of the body.
(B) Unmyelinated nerve fibres do not have Schwann cells which form the myelin sheath.
(C ) Axonal membrane of a neuron when not conducting any impulse is comparatively more permeable to potassium ions (K⁺)than to sodium ions (Na⁺).
(D) A synapse is formed by the membranes of a pre-synaptic neuron and a post-synaptic neuron.
s: C is correct: a resting axonal membrane is more permeable to K⁺ than to Na⁺. D is correct: a synapse is formed by the membranes of the pre-synaptic and post-synaptic neurons. A is wrong because the autonomic system supplies involuntary organs and smooth muscles. B is wrong because unmyelinated fibres are also enclosed by Schwann cells, which simply do not form myelin. So C and D are correct.

t: Which of the following are properties of neurons?
s: Neurons are excitable cells. They respond to stimuli by changing their membrane potential (excitability), and they carry the resulting impulse along their length to other cells (conductivity). These are the two key properties of nerve tissue. Elasticity is a property of connective tissue and flexibility is not a characteristic property of neurons, so the other options are wrong.

t: Resting membrane potential is
s: At rest the inside of the axon membrane is negative compared with the outside, and the potential difference is about -70 mV. -55 mV is roughly the threshold that must be reached to fire an action potential. +30 mV is close to the peak of the action potential, when the polarity is reversed. +70 mV is not a physiological value.

t: Resting membrane potential of a neuron exists mainly due to

K⁺ diffuses out and leaves non-diffusible negative proteins inside, which makes the inside negative (about -70 mV). The Na⁺-K⁺ pump keeps the gradients unequal, so A is wrong. High Na⁺ permeability is seen during depolarisation. Cl⁻ transport is not the main cause.

t:
Steps in synaptic conduction are given below
1. Synaptic vesicles release neurotransmitters.
2. Arrival of action potential in synaptic knob.
3. Neurotransmitters bind to specific receptors.
4.Release of Ca-ions into synaptic knob and adheres to synaptic vesicles.
5.Post synaptic membrane is repolarised by inactivating neurotransmitter
6.Regeneration of a new action potential on the post synaptic membrane.
The correct sequence of events is given by
s: First the action potential reaches the synaptic knob (2). Ca²⁺ then enters the knob and acts on the vesicles (4). The vesicles fuse with the membrane and release neurotransmitter (1). The neurotransmitter binds to its receptors (3), and a new action potential is produced in the post-synaptic membrane (6). Finally the neurotransmitter is inactivated and the membrane repolarises (5). The sequence is 2→4→1→3→6→5.

t: During chemical synaptic transmission ,a new action potential is regenerated on:
s: At a chemical synapse the neurotransmitter crosses the cleft and binds to receptors on the post-synaptic membrane. The synaptic cleft is only a fluid-filled gap, the pre-synaptic membrane releases the transmitter, and the vesicles only store it.

t: Neurons are considered as excitable cells because
s: Neurons are excitable because their membranes are kept in a polarised state at rest: inside negative, outside positive, at about -70 mV. Because the membrane stays polarised, a stimulus can quickly change its permeability and set off depolarisation. Membranes are not always depolarised, conduction is ionic rather than true electrical conduction, and they are permeable to ions through channels.

t: The cerebral cortex contains
s: The cerebral cortex is grey matter. It has motor areas that control voluntary movement and sensory areas that receive sensations. It also has large association areas, which are neither purely sensory nor motor and carry out complex functions such as intersensory association, memory and communication. t: Hypothalamic hormones are secreted by
s: The hypothalamus has groups of neurosecretory cells (hypothalamic nuclei) that produce hormones. These include releasing and inhibiting hormones that control the pituitary, as well as oxytocin and vasopressin. Glial cells, Schwann cells and oligodendrocytes are supporting cells. t: Cerebral aqueduct is found in
s: The cerebral aqueduct, also called the iter or aqueduct of Sylvius, is a narrow canal that passes through the midbrain. It connects the third ventricle of the forebrain with the fourth ventricle of the hindbrain. So it lies in the midbrain, not in the forebrain or hindbrain itself.

t: A neuron shows accumulation of waste and cellular debris. Which glial cell is likely absent?
s: Microglia are the resident macrophages of the CNS. They engulf and remove dead cells, waste and debris by phagocytosis, so if waste builds up, microglia are likely missing. Astrocytes give structural and metabolic support and form the blood-brain barrier. Oligodendrocytes form myelin. Ependymal cells line the ventricles and help produce CSF.

t: Which lobe of the cerebrum is responsible for processing auditory information?
s: The temporal lobe has the primary auditory cortex and Wernicke's area, so it processes sounds and helps understand language. The frontal lobe handles motor control and reasoning. The occipital lobe processes vision. The parietal lobe processes touch, temperature, pain and other body sensations.

t: After head trauma, a patient is unable to control body temperature and shows signs of extreme thirst. The affected brain region is:
s: The hypothalamus has the thermoregulatory centre and the thirst and hunger centres. It also produces ADH, which controls water balance. Damage to it can cause loss of temperature control and extreme thirst. The pons helps regulate breathing, the cerebellum coordinates movement and balance, and the midbrain handles visual and auditory reflexes.
